主要内容: Jim Cramer, host of 'Mad Money,' suggested that the post-earnings decline in Estee Lauder shares presents a buying opportunity. Despite a 5% drop in the stock following the earnings report, Cramer downplayed concerns about a slowdown in the company's business in China. He argued that when China ends its lockdowns, demand for Estee Lauder products is expected to soar. The company reported 11% organic sales growth and 14% revenue growth for its fiscal second quarter, surpassing Wall Street's expectations. Cramer emphasized that Chinese demand is the key factor, not supply constraints, and noted that consumers purchased Estee Lauder products when stores were open. Cramer's charitable trust sold its 100-share position in Estee Lauder in December at around $365.67 per share.
